opti-1: Long ago, ships and armies fought over this little Florida town.
opti-2: Spain built a stone fort to guard it.
opti-3: Look closer. The walls are made of shells.
opti-5: In 1740, enemy cannons fired at the fort for 27 days.
opti-6: The cannonballs bounced off, or sank into the soft shell rock.
opti-7: More than 300 years later, the walls still stand.
opti-8: How do scientists describe and compare different kinds of matter?
26-01-welcome: Our film starts at an old Florida fort with a secret in its walls. First, inspect a strange rock from the coast.
26-01-lesson: Today you're a materials scientist. Turn shells into stone, test two rocks, then climb a hardness ladder.
26-01-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
26-01-assign: Time to show what you learned. Pick some properties, then tell us how you'd tell two objects apart.
how-26-01-compare: Put the marble under one tray and the water under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a tray. Press Run the test. Then swap.
how-26-01-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing step: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the mineral shows.
how-26-01-det: Pick three materials, one at a time. Tap a clue, then name its key property. Predict a job that fits, and watch it at work.
how-26-01-partc: Draw two objects side by side. Label one property they share and one property that is different.
